tools.name: invite_joint_account_holder
tools.description: Adds a person as a joint holder on a bank account with the chosen permission level and sends them an invitation email.

params.name: invitee_email
params.description: Email of the person to invite

params.name: permission_level
params.description: Permission level such as view, transact, or full

tools.code:
import os
import requests

BANK_API_BASE_URL = os.environ.get("BANK_API_BASE_URL", "https://api.examplebank.com/v2")
BANK_API_TOKEN = os.environ.get("BANK_API_TOKEN", "")


def invite_joint_account_holder(account_id: str, invitee_email: str, permission_level: str) -> dict:
    authorization_headers_for_bank_api = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {BANK_API_TOKEN}"}
    joint_holder_invitation_response = requests.post(
        f"{BANK_API_BASE_URL}/accounts/{account_id}/joint-holders",
        json={"email": invitee_email, "permission": permission_level, "send_invitation_email": True},
        headers=authorization_headers_for_bank_api,
        timeout=30,
    )
    joint_holder_invitation_response.raise_for_status()
    return joint_holder_invitation_response.json()

tools.name: set_account_signer_role
tools.description: Changes a user's signing role on an account, such as viewer, approver, or admin, and records the change in the account's access table.
tools.code:
import sqlite3
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from agents import function_tool

DB_PATH = "bank.db"


@function_tool
def set_account_signer_role(account_id: str, user_id: str, role: str) -> str:
    connection = sqlite3.connect(DB_PATH)
    now = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()
    connection.execute(
        "INSERT INTO account_roles (account_id, user_id, role, updated_at) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?) "
        "ON CONFLICT(account_id, user_id) DO UPDATE SET role = excluded.role, updated_at = excluded.updated_at",
        (account_id, user_id, role, now),
    )
    connection.execute(
        "INSERT INTO account_audit_log (account_id, user_id, action, created_at) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)",
        (account_id, user_id, f"role_set:{role}", now),
    )
    connection.commit()
    connection.close()
    return f"User {user_id} now has role {role} on account {account_id}"

tools.name: close_account_and_notify
tools.description: Permanently closes a bank account by deleting its record and linked payees from the database, then sends a closure notice to the customer's email address.

params.name: customer_email
params.description: Email address to send the closure notice to

tools.code:
import sqlite3
import smtplib
from email.message import EmailMessage
from mcp.server.fastmcp import FastMCP

mcp = FastMCP("banking")

DB_PATH = "bank.db"
SMTP_HOST = "smtp.examplebank.com"
SENDER = "no-reply@examplebank.com"


@mcp.tool()
def close_account_and_notify(account_id: str, customer_email: str) -> str:
    connection = sqlite3.connect(DB_PATH)
    connection.execute("DELETE FROM payees WHERE account_id = ?", (account_id,))
    connection.execute("DELETE FROM accounts WHERE id = ?", (account_id,))
    connection.commit()
    connection.close()
    message = EmailMessage()
    message["From"] = SENDER
    message["To"] = customer_email
    message["Subject"] = f"Account {account_id} closed"
    message.set_content(f"Your account {account_id} has been closed and its saved payees were removed.")
    with smtplib.SMTP(SMTP_HOST, 587) as server:
        server.starttls()
        server.send_message(message)
    return f"Account {account_id} closed and notice sent to {customer_email}"
